title: Place the guards where the damage happens
brief: The model will answer whatever it is given. Checks can stand on the way in, on retrieved content, on tool calls and on the way out. Which do you need, how many can the latency budget carry, and what may reach the user while text streams?

blocks.text: Five places a guard can stand

blocks.title: Guard points on a RAG request
blocks.alt: A user input passes an input guard, retrieval returns chunks that pass a retrieval guard, the model proposes a tool call that passes a tool call guard, the tool response passes a tool response guard, and the final answer passes an output guard before reaching the user.
blocks.caption: Foundry names four intervention points (input, tool call, tool response, output). NeMo Guardrails names five rail types (input, retrieval, dialog, execution, output).

blocks.title: How guards run in the request path
blocks.intro: Where a guard stands is one decision. Whether it blocks the request, races it or trails behind a stream is another. Nothing in the vendor pages checked on 2026-10-13 publishes guard latency, so every option here is measured, not assumed.

options.name: Sequential gate before the model
options.summary: Run the input guard, then call the model.
pros: No tokens are spent on blocked requests
cons: The guard's latency adds in series
options.bestWhen: Blocked requests are common or generation is costly.
options.avoidWhen: The latency budget is tight and blocks are rare.

options.name: Parallel with generation
options.summary: Start the guard and the model together, cancel generation if the guard blocks.
pros: Hides the guard's latency behind the model call
Independent guards add only the slowest one
cons: Wasted tokens when the guard blocks
No tool side effects until the verdict arrives
options.bestWhen: Blocks are rare and the budget is tight.
options.avoidWhen: Generation triggers tools or other side effects.

meta.v: about the slowest guard, minus overlap

options.name: Buffered streaming (Azure default)
options.summary: Buffer completion text, filter each buffer and return content chunks.
pros: Violating text is stopped before it is sent
cons: Chunky streaming, not token by token
options.bestWhen: Harm if text leaks is high.
options.avoidWhen: Smooth token streaming is a hard product requirement.

options.name: Asynchronous filter (Azure)
options.summary: Stream token by token and deliver annotations in separate messages with offsets.
cons: The stop signal is guaranteed only within about a 1,000-character window, so violating text can reach the user first
Changing the mode needs permission to modify content filtering policies
options.bestWhen: Brief exposure is tolerable and you can retract or hide content.

blocks.title: Pick a guard stack
blocks.prompt: Flip the risk tier, the latency budget and how the answer is delivered.

options.name: Deterministic checks only
options.summary: Schemas, allow lists, regex, size limits.

options.name: Platform filters on input and output
options.summary: Harm categories, Prompt Shields, protected material.

options.name: Platform plus a groundedness check
options.summary: Adds a claim-level check on the answer.

options.name: Full path: input, retrieval, tools, output
LLM judge on every answer
options.summary: A second model reviews each answer against a policy.

low.why: Cheap and enough when harm is low.

mid.why: It misses semantic harms and ungrounded claims.

high.why: It cannot judge meaning, so it cannot carry a regulated assistant.

tight.why: Microseconds of work, no model call.

low.why: Defaults are enough and cost little.

mid.why: Covers the common harms and jailbreaks.

high.why: Necessary but not sufficient: no claim check and no tool scans by default.

tight.why: One classifier call, which you should measure, since no vendor figure is published.

stream.why: Default mode buffers chunks, asynchronous mode trades exposure for speed.

whole.why: Output checks run on the full text.

high.why: Adds an answer-level check, but still no tool coverage.

tight.why: Needs the finished answer and a second call.

stream.why: It must see the answer before judging it, so it conflicts with streaming.

whole.why: Checks run before anything is shown.

mid.why: Reasonable if documents or tools are untrusted.

high.why: Covers input, retrieved content, tool calls and output.

tight.why: Many guards, even in parallel, add the slowest of each stage.

low.why: Costs a full model call per answer for little gain.

high.why: Flexible for custom policy, but not deterministic.

tight.why: One extra full LLM call, roughly seconds (author estimate, not a vendor figure).

blocks.takeaway: Risk tier and delivery mode usually decide before latency does. Streaming and answer-level checks pull in opposite directions.

items.symptom: Policy-violating text flashes on screen and then disappears.
items.cause: Asynchronous filter mode streams first and signals the stop later, within about 1,000 characters.
items.fix: Use buffered streaming for high-risk surfaces, or hold display until the verdict. Detect with annotation offsets in logs.

items.symptom: p95 latency equals the sum of five guard calls.
items.fix: Run independent guards in parallel so you pay the slowest, and record per-guard timings.

items.symptom: Tool calls go unscanned even though the model deployment has strict filters.
items.cause: An agent's guardrail fully overrides its model's, and it has no tool call or tool response controls.
items.fix: Add tool call and tool response controls (preview) to the agent's guardrail and test with a tool-bound attack.

items.symptom: A poisoned PDF steers the model although the user prompt was clean.
items.cause: Only user input was scanned. The attack arrived through retrieved content.
items.fix: Scan retrieved chunks and tool responses for document attacks and treat them as untrusted.

items.cause: A timeout is treated as a pass, which fails open.
items.fix: Choose fail closed or degrade to abstain per risk tier, and alert on guard timeouts.

blocks.title: Estimates in this level
blocks.md: Vendors publish no guard latency numbers on the pages checked 2026-10-13. As a planning estimate only, a classifier call costs tens to a few hundred milliseconds and an LLM judge adds one full model call. Replace both with your own p50 and p95 measurements.

quiz.q: Match each threat to the earliest guard placement that can stop it.

pairs.l: A user types a jailbreak prompt
Instructions hidden in a retrieved PDF
An agent proposes a destructive API call

quiz.explain: Each threat is only visible at one point. A clean user prompt hides the PDF attack, a tool call exists before any output, and lyrics only appear in the completion. That is why a single guard on input is not a stack.

quiz.q: A team switches Azure content filtering to the asynchronous filter mode to cut latency. Which statement is true?
options: Annotations arrive before any text is streamed, so nothing is shown first
The filter buffers each chunk, so no violating text can ever be shown
Some violating text can be displayed before the stop signal arrives
The mode removes the need to configure any guardrail for the deployment
quiz.explain: Asynchronous filter streams token by token and sends annotations in separate messages, so some violating text can be displayed before the stop signal, which is guaranteed only within about a 1,000-character window. The default mode is the one that buffers and filters each chunk. Guardrails still need configuring, and annotations follow the text, they do not precede it.

quiz.q: Treat these p95 times as additive. Retrieval 400 ms, model 1,600 ms, input guard 120 ms. Three independent output guards take 80, 150 and 200 ms. Run in parallel, what is the total request latency?
quiz.hint: Parallel guards add only the slowest one
quiz.explain: Input guard 120 + retrieval 400 + model 1,600 + the slowest output guard 200 = 2,320 ms. Run in series the output guards add 430 ms and the total is 2,550 ms. Summing p95 values is a planning shortcut, so confirm with a measured end-to-end p95.

takeaways: A guard only sees what passes its placement, so cover input, retrieved content, tools and output
Independent guards run in parallel add the slowest, not the sum
Asynchronous filter trades latency for brief exposure, with the stop signal guaranteed only within about 1,000 characters
An agent's guardrail replaces its model's guardrail, so check tool coverage explicitly
